newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast bans trade in ivory tusks.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast bans trade in ivory tusks.

text.p: Ivory Coast, which tags itself the Elephant of Africa in its pursuit of economic growth, has banned all trade in ivory tusks and ordered a nationwide census of all tusks as part of efforts to protect the elephant.

A government statement, published on Saturday, said President Henri Konan Bedie had ordered the crackdown plus strict controls on the traffic of tusks into and out of the country in a decree signed at a cabinet meeting on Friday.

"This decree aims to limit the threat to the elephant, the world's largest terrestrial mammal, which has been exploited over the past three decades in Africa in general and in Ivory Coast in particular," it added.
The statement said the decree targeted tusks that were poached or smuggled but was intended to ensure that legally held tusks could be displayed with due dignity.
It said the ban would remain in force "until the situation in the country allowed other dispositions".
Bedie himself has tusks on display at his official residence.
